_meta.description: Holdout query set for search_memory's mode="strict" relevance-abstention gate (memory_service.accept_or_abstain / _resolve_supersession_chains -- see plans/scalable-strolling-stallman.md Part D and SALTMDB memory `9c199005`/`c27792a1`/`b9b75764`). Companion to golden_queries.json (which is a positive-only, top-1/top-k ranking-quality set) -- this file exercises mode="strict"-specific behavior: abstention on no-evidence queries, acceptance on genuinely grounded ones, and supersession-chain substitution.
_meta.corpus: scripts/benchmarking/build_diverse_test_db.py's output (scratch/diverse_corpus_full.db, ~21.7k entities, 76 real `supersedes` edges) -- deliberately NOT the live personal corpus (per the standing SALTMDB_DB_PATH dev rule): run every case here against a throwaway COPY of that file, never the file itself and never the live default DB.
_meta.provenance: Every case was run live against scratch/diverse_corpus_full.db during Part A-D implementation/verification (2026-08) and the expected_outcome below reflects the actual measured result at that time, not a guess. See run_relevance_gate_holdout.py in this directory for the runner that reproduces these checks.
_meta.known_gaps_codex_review: Codex's implementation review (post-Part-E) correctly flagged that this file has no case for the semantic_paraphrase_positive category described below, and none for a broad-theme near-miss, a tied-candidate fork, or a stale-successor re-check. These were deliberately NOT added here after investigation: at this corpus's real ~21.7k-entity, heavily-multilingual scale, genuine hand-built paraphrase queries with disjoint vocabulary from a target entity were empirically found to usually land at BROADLY_RELATED_THEMES (0.63-0.74), not the stricter SAME_SPECIFIC_TOPIC bar the gate requires -- the one query found during investigation that DID clear SAME_SPECIFIC_TOPIC also turned out to share enough vocabulary with its target to independently pass via the FTS-only rule anyway, so it would not have exercised the semantic-only tier specifically. Mining a real, reliable, non-flaky case of this exact shape out of noisy real corpus data is impractical with the time available; the shape is instead covered precisely and deterministically by tests/test_relevance_gate.py's engineered-fixture unit tests (test_strict_mode_keeps_semantic_only_candidate_with_same_specific_topic, test_semantic_only_broadly_related_rejected) and tests/test_supersession_resolution.py's fork/tie-break tests (test_genuine_mid_chain_fork_tie_break, test_fork_tie_break_falls_back_to_created_at_then_id) -- see run_relevance_gate_holdout.py's own module docstring for the same reasoning.

case_meanings.nonsense_abstain: A query with no real relation to anything in the corpus. Expected outcome: mode="strict" returns []. NOTE (documented, not hidden -- matches this codebase's stated risk-asymmetry convention): at this corpus's real ~21.7k-entity scale, a small residual false-accept rate remains for nonsense queries that happen to land within the calibrated SAME_SPECIFIC_TOPIC chunk-topic tier of some unrelated document purely by chance (measured ~2/7 to ~3/7 on the specific gibberish strings below during verification) -- see accept_or_abstain's own docstring for the full investigation of why a raw-distance/margin cutoff was tried first and rejected, and why this residual rate is the accepted trade-off rather than a bug. `held_out: true` cases are exactly the ones known to sometimes flip; they still count as a real check (report the actual outcome), just don't re-tune any threshold to force them to always abstain.
case_meanings.fts_exact_positive: A query built from exact, distinctive terms known to appear verbatim in a specific entity's title/content -- expected to be accepted via the FTS-only or dual-channel DIRECT rule (a real term match, not dependent on the semantic-only tier at all).
case_meanings.semantic_paraphrase_positive: A query that paraphrases a real entity with deliberately low vocabulary overlap. Expected to be accepted ONLY if it independently clears the SAME_SPECIFIC_TOPIC chunk-topic tier -- a weaker/broader paraphrase legitimately abstaining here is NOT a failure, it is the accepted false-reject cost of this gate's design (see accept_or_abstain's docstring). No case of this category exists in this file yet -- see known_gaps_codex_review above for why, and where the shape IS covered instead.
case_meanings.supersession_substitution: A query that lexically/semantically matches an OLD entity that is the target of a real, currently-valid `supersedes` edge in this corpus. Expected outcome: mode="strict" substitutes to the NEW (source) entity and does NOT return the old target id at all.
